# South Andrews Healthcare and Mobility Hub — One-Page Summary

**901–917 South Andrews Avenue, Fort Lauderdale, Florida** · Prepared 2026-07-27

> **external_use_status: internal_only — BLOCKED for external distribution.** Gated behind [External Publication Checklist](EXTERNAL_PUBLICATION_CHECKLIST.md) and [Document Update Order](../planning/Document%20Update%20Order.md) Step 8. See [Institutional Development Prospectus](Institutional%20Development%20Prospectus.md) for the full blocker list.

---

**The site.** A 38,207 SF (0.88-acre) corner with 275 ft on South Andrews Avenue and 170 ft on SW 9th Street, in Fort Lauderdale's hospital corridor. Hardy Park protects the north edge permanently. Ten minutes' walk to downtown, 2.8 miles to the airport, within a federal Qualified Opportunity Zone. Zoned RAC-RPO; entirely within FEMA Zone AE; currently three 1959-era commercial buildings. **The sponsor does not own the property — this is a prospective acquisition.**

**The proposal.** A healthcare-anchored building: medical retail at the street, flexible clinical and medical-office space above, structured parking, and mobility infrastructure sized as an enabler rather than a business. Recommended scheme is **four storeys, 108,000 GSF, 20,400 RSF clinical, 12,000 RSF medical retail, 169 stalls — approximately $40.9M core development cost including land.**

**Why four storeys.** It sits below the discretionary height-review threshold, parks itself with a modest surplus, needs only a conventional 480 V electrical service, carries the most defensible use argument, and is built to grow vertically later. Larger schemes add capital and risk without adding return: every increment of vertical scale earns between 2.12% and 3.43% on the incremental capital.

**What the numbers say.** Both current models show the base project failing its return requirements — yields on cost of 2.7%–4.1% against a 7.0% hurdle. A residual analysis prepared for this package establishes that **the shortfall is not curable by the acquisition price: at a land basis of zero, no scenario exceeds 4.49% yield on cost.** The office rent required to reach 7.0% is roughly $131/RSF against $50 modelled.

**What that means.** The site is right, the thesis is right, and the programme is too large for the price. The project becomes investable with a healthcare anchor, public capital, or a transaction structure that removes the fixed land obligation — not by negotiating the land price.

**Mobility, stated accurately.** No autonomous-vehicle, fleet, or charging revenue is underwritten anywhere. Gross stalls are not fleet capacity: after the building's own code-required parking, the largest scheme tested yields roughly **140 operational fleet positions, not 300–400**, at approximately **$545,000 per usable position.** The operating model therefore splits across two sites — South Andrews as a high-throughput transfer point, overnight storage and servicing at a lower-cost industrial depot. That split cuts the required electrical service from ~3,208 kW to ~1,143 kW, avoiding medium-voltage service and roughly $3M of capital. **No depot site has been identified or secured.**

**Minimum to make the site function.** Approximately **$5.0M excluding land** — demolition, environmental allowance, flood and stormwater work, paving, power, 40 managed chargers, passenger-transfer canopy, and streetscape — makes South Andrews operable as a staging and implementation ground with no autonomous-vehicle deployment at all.

**Next steps.** A bounded pre-acquisition diligence programme of roughly **$100,000–$200,000**, all completable before any land commitment: recover the referenced Phase I and Phase II environmental reports; obtain an FPL preliminary load letter; commission land-use counsel and a City pre-application; complete an architectural and parking test-fit; validate medical-office rents; obtain contractor pricing. Two of these could independently change the answer.

**Status.** No entitlement. No confirmed utility capacity. No committed partner of any kind. No financing. No approved design. All costs are AACE Class 5 planning estimates (−30%/+50%) with no contractor pricing behind them. Every figure is a planning-level estimate or model output, not a verified fact or a guaranteed result. Feasibility is not established.
